title: Introduce attestation-anchor RBAC v2 rejector and KMS residency verifier
author: Hannah Park
description: Adds a new attestation-anchor based RBAC v2 rejector and a lightweight KMS residency verifier used by policy decision flow and audit pipelines. Motivation: customers with strict data residency requirements reported edge cases where operator tokens or downstream KMS calls carried ambiguous region claims and audits could not reliably correlate key usage to tenant residency. This PR implements 1) attestation-anchor: an optional decision gate that verifies a signed attestation blob from upstream operator-token issuers and rejects requests when attestation does not match the tenant's pinned residency profile, 2) kms-residency-verifier: a synchronous verifier that checks KMS key metadata and remote-region provenance headers before allowing encryption/decryption calls, 3) audit-consistency-probe: a low-overhead verifier that writes a signed audit proof event when KMS residency differs from the request's claimed region to help downstream forensics, 4) config/rollout flags and feature gates for staged canary enabling and backwards-compatible fallback to previous behavior. Included migration steps, a Linear task list, and a short CLI tool to regressively validate tenant residency mappings. This is implemented behind an opt-in feature gate 'attestation_anchor_v1' and a service config flag 'kms_residency_enforce' that can be toggled per environment. Backwards compatibility: when both flags are false the runtime path is unchanged. Testing and verification: unit tests for attestation parsing and policy rule matching, integration tests with a fake KMS metadata service, e2e smoke tests that assert audit proof emission, and load-tested guarded path to ensure <5% median p50 latency regression under synthetic workloads. Rollout plan: enable in internal infra, dark-launch to 5% traffic, then 25% across regions with cross-checking turned on, then full enable after two days of stable telemetry. Related work: references ENG-4928 for long-term RBAC stability, SUP-1123 for customer support ticket, and SEC-317 design doc. Documentation: includes a new doc on operator attestation format and admin guide for tuning residency heuristics.

review_comments: Priya Menon: Can we make the attestation signature verification pluggable so enterprise teams can bring their own verifier?
Luis Ortega: The residency verifier hits KMS metadata in the hot path; we should ensure it does not stall downstream RPCs. Can we cache negative results with TTL?
Daniel Kim: Minor nit: prefer explicit error enums for audit probe failures so SLO diagnostics can group them, not string matches.
Aisha Reddy: Approve pending a migration note explaining the operator token backwards compatibility and an admin flag to disable audit proof emission for PII-sensitive tenants.
author_responses: Hannah Park: Pluggable verifier added via an interface and default implementation kept in this PR; docs updated with extension points.
Hannah Park: Added an in-memory negative cache with a 2m TTL and metrics for miss/evict counts. Also added a fallback fast-path that skips verifier when 'kms_residency_enforce' is false.
Hannah Park: Replaced string error paths with typed error codes and added mapping to telemetry fields.
Hannah Park: Added migration note and admin flag 'audit_proof_emit' to disable proof emission for selected tenants; updated policy and docs.
release_notes: Introduce optional attestation-anchor RBAC gate and KMS residency verifier to strengthen tenant data residency enforcement. Feature is behind feature flags and disabled by default. Admins can enable audit proof emission to improve residency forensics.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in production turn on 'attestation_anchor_v1' in feature flags and incrementally enable 'kms_residency_enforce' via canary config. Monitor metric authz.attestation.reject_rate and audit.proof.emitted_count. If latency regressions exceed 10% consider increasing negative cache TTL or disabling enforcement temporarily.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover attestation parsing and verifier mocks. Integration test suite simulates KMS metadata responses and validates audit proof events. Load tests on perf canary show median p50 4% regression on canary machines with 500 concurrent requests, within target.
